cards.name: Vision cone that widens with alertness
cards.summary: An enemy sees a target only inside a view cone whose width grows with its alert state, and never beyond a long maximum distance.
cards.behavior: The cone starts from a per-character base field of view, 90 degrees for a standard soldier, and multiplies it by a factor chosen from the current alert state: 1.0 relaxed, 1.5 for query and alert, 2.0 in combat. So a relaxed guard sees a 90 degree cone, an alerted one 135 degrees and a fighting one 180 degrees. Yaw and pitch are each tested against half of the final angle, so the cone is as tall as it is wide. A scoped shooter narrows the cone to 80 percent. Any character that has already fought someone is widened to at least 270 degrees, and an alerted or fighting character that saw its target on the previous check uses a full 360 degrees so it keeps tracking. A target beyond the character reach attribute, 16000 units for ordinary enemies, is never seen at all. Only after this cheap test passes does the game spend line-of-sight traces.

constants.name: base field of view, standard soldier
constants.unit: degrees (full cone width), before state scaling

constants.name: field of view scale, query and alert
minimum cone after any previous fight

capabilities: full-circle tracking once a target is acquired
cheap angle and distance rejection before ray casts

cards.name: Multi-probe line of sight from the head
cards.summary: A visibility test casts up to five rays from the observer eye at different parts of the target body, using the animated head position.
cards.behavior: After the cone test, the game traces from the eye to the center of the target bounding box with a mask that ignores anything a bullet can pass through. If that ray is blocked it tries the bottom of the box, then the top, then two rays from eye positions shifted sideways by roughly half the target width. The first three probes are gated by a potential visibility set test, and the side probes run only when one of those passed, which saves traces in separate rooms. Water surfaces are traced through, so a swimmer is visible. Enemy eyes come from the animated head bone, pushed 12 units along its up axis, so a guard that turns its head sees in that direction. Right after a save is loaded the head bone is ignored for 4 seconds, and for 2 seconds the player stays unseen unless already spotted, which gives a safe settling window.

constants.name: eye offset along head bone up axis
head-bone eye delay after loading a save
player unseen window after loading a save

capabilities: body-part sampling to catch half-hidden targets
load-time grace so saves are not instantly punished

cards.name: Gunfire and bullet impact hearing
cards.summary: Each weapon shot broadcasts a noise radius, and idle enemies that hear a shot or a nearby bullet impact go to investigate.
cards.behavior: Firing records the weapon and position and calls an audible event whose range comes from a per-weapon table: a knife, Sten or silenced pistol only 64 units, pistols 700, submachine guns 1000, grenades 1500, the Mauser and its sniper variant 2000, dynamite 3000, while the Garand is nearly silent at 128. A listener multiplies the range by its hearing scale and tests squared distance first; outside the potential visibility set the range is cut by a further factor of 0.9. When the shooter is not itself in combat, listeners ignore it unless they could treat it as an enemy, so teammates are not alarmed by each other. A hit stores the noise position and sets a reaction time 200 to 500 milliseconds ahead, and idle logic acts on it only while it is under 2 seconds old. Separately, every traced bullet is offered to idle enemies: they notice an impact within their detection radius of 512 units, or a bullet path passing within half that radius ahead of them, after a 100 to 300 ms delay. Enemies already in combat ignore impacts, and one that starts inspecting ignores further impacts for 5 seconds.

constants.name: hearing range, knife and silenced weapons
hearing range, Mauser and sniper rifle
hearing range scale outside the visibility set
noise reaction delay, base
constants.unit: milliseconds of level time, plus a random 0 to 299

capabilities: per-weapon noise radius for stealth play
silenced weapons that only travel a few units
investigation of shots and passing bullets

cards.name: Shared awareness, breadcrumbs and corpse discovery
cards.summary: Nearby teammates copy each other sightings, targets leave a short position trail, and finding a dead friend triggers an inspection.
cards.behavior: When an enemy sights a target it also looks at friendly teammates within 384 units and copies what they know when that is more recent, including the hostile flag, so one alerted soldier alerts the group. Teammates that are checked while idle are re-tested only every 2 to 3 seconds, or every half second to one second if the friend is fighting. A friend that is dead and not yet inspected is flagged for inspection, a friend in combat makes a calmer teammate investigate, and a friend that is merely alert pulls the observer up to alert too. While the target is out of view the game drops up to 3 breadcrumb positions, one per second of absence, and idle logic later sends the enemy back to hunt a previous target that has not been seen for 5 seconds.

constants.name: idle teammate recheck, base
constants.unit: milliseconds of level time, plus random 0 to 999

capabilities: last-seen breadcrumb trail for search behavior
enemies that react to bodies of allies

cards.name: Reaction delay before a sighting counts
cards.summary: A sighting only becomes usable after a per-character reaction time that shrinks for close or already engaged targets.
cards.behavior: The target must have been continuously visible for the full reaction time before the enemy treats it as seen. The delay is 1000 milliseconds times the reaction attribute: 0.5 for a soldier, 0.1 for a zombie, 0.6 for a heavy soldier, 0.8 for a loper beast. It is halved once the character has begun more than one standing attack, and when the target is closer than 384 units it is multiplied by 0.5 plus half the distance fraction, so point blank reaction is twice as fast. A glance shorter than the delay therefore never triggers anything, which lets a player dip in and out of view. Indirect queries add a memory: for 5 seconds after the target left view, the enemy is still treated as seeing it.
capabilities: short memory after a target ducks out of view

cards.name: Relaxed, query, alert and combat escalation
cards.summary: Enemies climb through relaxed, query, alert and combat states; a first glimpse starts a short suspicion timer before shooting begins.
cards.behavior: A visible character that is not yet hostile is only a possible enemy. A relaxed guard that sees one enters the query state, plays a look animation and locks onto it. On the first query within a one minute window the lock-on takes 1000 milliseconds, on the second 500 milliseconds, and from the third on the next sighting goes straight to combat. If the target leaves view during the lock-on the timer is zeroed, so the next moment it is visible escalates to combat at once; a shot fired by the target during the query does the same, and a query with nothing seen ends back in relaxed. An enemy inside the inner detection radius of 512 units, or any enemy once the observer is alert, is marked hostile immediately and sends a relaxed guard directly to combat. Taking damage always raises a calmer enemy to alert, and soldiers spawn relaxed while monsters spawn alert.

constants.name: inner detection radius
constants.unit: world units (times 10 while a shooter is scoped)

cards.name: Aggression score and take-cover decision
cards.summary: A single willingness score built from health, recent pain, distance and reloading decides whether an enemy chases or hides.
cards.behavior: The score starts at 1.0 and is reduced when health is below 50, with a larger penalty for timid characters. Recent damage subtracts three times the timidity multiplied by the fraction of a memory window that remains, where the window is 15000 milliseconds minus 10000 times the aggression attribute squared. A distance term adds (distance minus 800) over 8000, and an active weapon reload subtracts its remaining time in seconds. The result is multiplied by the aggression attribute and floored at zero. A character chases when the attribute is exactly 1.0 or the score exceeds 0.6. It takes cover when the score times an engagement factor falls below 0.4; the factor is 1.2 while attacking, 0.8 otherwise, tripled while following a leader and cut to 0.6 for a tactical, stationary character when the player aim ray is within about 14 degrees. An idle smart enemy that can be seen first tries to hide for 2 to 5 seconds, preferring to crouch where only standing exposes it.

constants.name: pain memory window, base
constants.unit: milliseconds of level time, minus 10000 times aggression squared

constants.name: player aim dodge cosine
constants.unit: dot product of aim and direction

constants.name: hide duration, base
constants.unit: milliseconds of level time, plus random 0 to 2999

capabilities: courage that falls with damage and recovers over time
cover seeking tied to a single score

cards.name: Enemy aim that sharpens the longer you stay visible
cards.summary: Enemy shot spread depends on a base accuracy plus a bonus that ramps up while the player stays continuously in view.
cards.behavior: Each character has a base accuracy: 0.5 for a soldier, 0.7 for a zombie, 1.0 for a heavy soldier. While the enemy keeps the player continuously in view this value ramps by up to plus or minus 0.2 over a window of 500 milliseconds plus 3500 times one minus the skill scale (game skill divided by three), then clamps between zero and one. Each bullet endpoint is offset at the end of an 8192 unit trace by up to (1 minus accuracy) times 2048 sideways and 1.25 times that vertically, on top of weapon spread. The aim point also wobbles along the target velocity with a slow sine for targets farther than 256 units, and a character with aim skill over 0.2 leads a moving target by 0.2 times its skill in seconds. Grenades are aimed at the feet inside 180 units and lobbed higher beyond 400.

constants.name: accuracy ramp window, base
constants.unit: milliseconds of level time, plus 3500 times (1 minus skill scale)

constants.name: accuracy ramp swing
constants.unit: total change in accuracy, plus or minus 0.2 about the base

constants.name: maximum aim offset
constants.unit: world units at a trace length of 8192

constants.name: target lead factor
constants.unit: seconds times aim skill, only above skill 0.2

capabilities: enemies that start inaccurate and warm up

cards.name: Damage quota flinch and stun
cards.summary: Enemies only flinch after accumulated damage crosses a threshold that decays over time, with extra weight on the first hit after a lull.
cards.behavior: Every hit adds its damage to a quota. The quota drains each second by (1 plus skill over 3) times (7.5 plus attack skill times 10). If more than a second has passed since the last flinch, the new hit is multiplied by up to 1 plus 4 times (1 minus half the skill scale), so the first shot after a lull staggers easily. When the quota passes 25 times the character pain scale, the enemy plays a pain animation, and if a single hit exceeded 30 times the scale a coin flip upgrades it to a stun. The enemy then stops moving and firing for the animation length plus 250 milliseconds, the quota resets and further flinches are blocked for that pause plus up to a second on hard skill. Fire always flinches (threshold 1, never stunned). A heavy soldier has a scale of 2, so it needs twice the damage to be interrupted.

constants.name: pain threshold
constants.unit: damage quota points, times character pain scale

constants.name: stun threshold
constants.unit: single-hit damage, times character pain scale

constants.name: quota decay base
constants.unit: points per second, plus 10 times attack skill

constants.name: lull scaling cap
constants.unit: seconds of gap that count toward the multiplier

capabilities: flinch from accumulated damage rather than every hit

cards.name: Heavy armored super soldier
cards.summary: A slow, high-health enemy with an automatic weapon, perfect aim, knife immunity, armor plates that fall off and a shaking footstep.
cards.behavior: The heavy soldier has 300 health, an aim accuracy of 1.0, and a pain scale of 2, so it flinches only after twice the usual damage. It cannot be knifed, takes no lightning damage and no flame damage until most of its armor is gone, and never overheats its automatic gun. Armor is cosmetic and tied to health: the number of plates removed is the fraction of health lost times 14, plates fall at random, and flame protection ends once five sixths of the plates are gone. With its automatic weapon it keeps advancing while the player is more than 300 units away or has not been hurt for 3 seconds. Each footstep triggers a camera shake near the player that reaches 800 units.

constants.name: pain threshold scale
constants.unit: multiplier on pain and stun thresholds

constants.name: chase distance for the automatic weapon
lightning weapon reach of the boss

capabilities: footstep camera shake for large enemies

cards.name: Zombie that rises once, then gibs
cards.summary: The first death of a zombie class enemy is temporary, and it stands back up with reduced health after a few seconds.
cards.behavior: When a zombie dies the first time it lies down and sets a rebirth timer of 5000 milliseconds plus a random 0 to 1999. If the level flag for no revive is set, or this is already its second death, it gibs instead. At the timer the game checks that the body area is free of solid entities, so a player standing on it delays the rise. It then restores health to its starting value minus 50, with a floor of 30, plays a get-up animation and thinks again. Zombies are immune to headshots, and bullets cannot gib an enemy, with health stopping just above minus 40, except for a zombie or fire from the heavy automatic weapon. Any non-bullet hit above 20 damage, such as an explosion, gibs a zombie at once and skips the revive.

constants.name: rebirth delay, base
constants.unit: milliseconds of level time, plus random 0 to 1999

constants.name: explosion gib damage
constants.unit: damage per hit that gibs a zombie outright

capabilities: blocked rise while the spot is occupied

cards.name: Multi-hit zombie melee swings
cards.summary: A zombie melee attack plays one of five animations that land one to three timed hits of 12 to 20 damage at short reach.
cards.behavior: One of five attack animations is picked. Each defines one to three hit times measured from the animation start, for example 11 frames at 20 per second for the first. When a hit time passes, the game traces a short melee reach, 44 units plus 4, and deals that animation damage only if the first thing hit is the intended target: 16, 16, 16, 12 and 20 for the five animations. A hit and a miss play different sounds. Between hits the zombie keeps facing its target, and if the predicted target position is more than 16 units away after allowing for both body radii it frees its legs from the attack animation and walks forward, so a retreating player is followed through the swing.

constants.name: melee reach
constants.unit: world units, plus 4 for the trace

cards.name: Zombie flame breath and spirit attacks
cards.summary: Zombies have two ranged special attacks: a short burst of fire and a slow-charging skull projectile that blocks overlapping casts.
cards.behavior: The fire attack starts when the target is within the flame radius minus 50 units. The radius is 0.3 of the 1250 unit flamethrower range, so about 325 units to begin. It lasts 4000 milliseconds, keeps the zombie facing the target with the aim pitched 20 degrees down, and ends early if the target leaves the radius. A zombie that has a flame weapon is immune to flame damage. The spirit attack has a range of 1000 units and a 6000 millisecond build-up with a 1000 millisecond fade-out. It is aborted when the zombie loses direct sight of the target. A spirit cannot start within one second of another one beginning anywhere in the level, so a group never casts in lockstep.

constants.name: flame radius scale
constants.unit: fraction of the 1250 unit flamethrower range

constants.name: flame start margin
constants.unit: world units inside the flame radius

constants.name: spirit cooldown between starts
constants.unit: milliseconds of level time, shared across all zombies

cards.name: Player ground speed, friction and crouch
cards.summary: Ground movement uses a base speed of 320 scaled to run and crouch, with Quake-style friction and acceleration.
cards.behavior: The server sets the base speed to 320 units per second. Input is normalised so diagonals are not faster, then multiplied by 0.8 for a run (256 units per second) or 1.1 while sprinting with stamina (352). A crouch clamps the wish speed to 0.25 of the base, 80 units per second, and wading in water to 0.5 at full depth. Friction removes 6 times the larger of the current speed or 100 per second, so low speeds stop quickly. Acceleration adds 10 times the wish speed per second up to the target speed. On slick ground or while being knocked back it drops to 1, so control is lost. AI characters have backward and sideways input clamped to half strength, so they move slower in those directions.

constants.name: ground friction
constants.unit: per second, applied to max(speed, stop speed)

capabilities: run, sprint and crouch speed tiers
loss of control when knocked back

cards.name: Jump impulse and sprint stamina
cards.summary: A fixed jump impulse with a short retrigger delay, plus a stamina bar that sprinting and jumping drain and standing still refills.
cards.behavior: A jump needs the button held and released since the last one, at least 500 milliseconds since the previous jump, and sets vertical speed to 270 units per second, which under gravity 800 rises about 45 units. Each jump takes 2000 from a 20000 stamina bar. Sprinting only works while more than 50 stamina remains and drains 50 per movement update, but only when speed is above 128 so standing against a wall costs nothing. The bar refills at 500 per second when not sprinting, doubles above 5000 and stacks with a further 500 per second when the player holds still. Sprinting is not allowed while crouched or in water. The result is that stamina limits repeated jumps and long chases more than fights.

constants.name: sprint stamina drain
constants.unit: stamina units per movement update, rate unverified

cards.name: Fall damage tiers with stun
cards.summary: Landing speed squared selects one of five damage tiers up to a lethal fall, each with a short stun, and water softens it.
cards.behavior: On landing the exact impact speed is solved from the fall distance and gravity, then squared and multiplied by 0.0001 to form a delta. Up to 7 only a footstep plays, silent when crouched or walking, and above 7 a short-fall sound plays with no damage. Higher values pick a tier: above 38.75 deals 10, above 48 deals 15, above 58 deals 25, above 67 deals 50 and above 77 kills with 9999. Tier 10, 15 and 50 stun the player for 1000 milliseconds and tier 25 for 250 by zeroing velocity under knockback control, and landing on slick ground suppresses the stun. Standing water multiplies the delta by 0.5 at waist depth and 0.25 at chest depth, and complete submersion cancels it. Each hurt tier also adds a camera shake that grows with the tier. First damage starts at an impact speed near 620 units per second and death near 880.

cards.name: Knife stealth kill from behind
cards.summary: The knife kills ordinary human enemies in one hit when the player stands behind them within 48 units, ignoring their alertness.
cards.behavior: Every frame the server traces the crosshair ray. With the knife selected and a standard human enemy on the cursor, it compares the forward vectors of the player and the target. If their dot product exceeds 0.9, so both face about the same way within 26 degrees, a knife hint appears within 48 units. A knife swing in that state deals 100 damage with a special stealth means of death, while a normal hit deals 5 plus a random 0 to 4. The enemy alert state is not tested at all, so being behind is the only requirement. Heavy soldiers and the large boss take no knife damage, and the swing repeats every 200 milliseconds.
capabilities: aim hint when a stab is possible

cards.name: Fire interval, clip and overheat table
cards.summary: Each weapon has a table row with its shot interval, clip size, reload time and optional heat limit.
cards.behavior: After every shot the weapon timer grows by the next-shot time from the table. Pistols use 400 milliseconds, the MP40 100, the Thompson 120, the Sten 110, the Mauser and Garand 1200, the sniper rifle 1700, the rocket launcher 2000 and grenades 1600. The automatic gun with 500 rounds fires every 45 milliseconds so that it locks to the server frame. A weapon with a heat limit adds heat per shot and cools at a fixed rate; at the limit it overheats and cannot fire for 2000 milliseconds, but heavy soldier characters skip this. Clip size and reload time are separate, for example 32 rounds and 2600 milliseconds for the MP40. A short delay of 100 milliseconds sits between the trigger and the first bullet for most guns.

cards.name: Aim spread bloom from firing and turning
cards.summary: A spread value from 0 to 255 grows with each shot and with fast view turns, recovers over time, and scales every bullet cone.
cards.behavior: The spread meter recovers at 200 per second divided by a per-weapon recovery scale, 0.4 for a Thompson and 10 for a sniper rifle, and the scale is halved while crouched on the ground so recovery doubles. Turning the view adds spread once the turn speed passes a dead zone of 30 degrees per second divided by the weapon scale, ramping to 800 per second at 150 degrees per second divided by the scale, and scoped weapons also count walking speed as turning. Each shot adds three times a per-weapon amount: 35 for a Luger, 50 for a Mauser, 15 to 24 for submachine guns. Zooming pins the meter at 255. The server divides the meter by 255 and adds a floor of 0.15, or 0.4 for pistols, so a fully steady player is still imperfect. That fraction multiplies the weapon base cone, such as 600 for the Luger or 1200 for the Thompson, when firing.

constants.name: spread recovery rate
constants.unit: meter units per second, divided by weapon scale

constants.name: spread growth rate from turning
constants.unit: meter units per second at full turn speed

capabilities: accuracy that rewards standing still and crouching
bloom per shot and per view turn

cards.name: Per-weapon damage, headshots and knockback
cards.summary: Fixed per-shot damage by weapon, a double-damage headshot with instant kills on ordinary humans, and capped knockback.
cards.behavior: Single-player damage is a switch on weapon: Luger 6, Colt 8, MP40 6, Mauser 20, sniper rifle 55, rocket 200. A head hit within 1024 units from a rifle or pistol class weapon doubles damage; against ordinary human soldiers and civilians a player head hit sets damage to 200 so it is a kill. The Garand and its scope kill the same enemies with any body hit. Monster types such as zombies take no head hits, and a helmeted guard must lose the helmet to a first head hit before the next one kills. Knockback is the damage capped at 60, scaled by a global factor of 1000 over a mass of 200, applied as velocity and a knockback state of 50 to 200 milliseconds. Explosions are scaled on the player by skill: 0.25, 0.75 and 0.9.

constants.name: sniper rifle damage
constants.unit: health points per hit, single player

constants.name: Mauser damage
constants.unit: health points per hit, single player

constants.name: headshot kill damage on common humans

capabilities: capped knockback and brief loss of control

cards.name: Distance-faded camera shake
cards.summary: Up to four timed shakes, each fading with distance and time, are combined into a pitch, yaw and roll wobble.
cards.behavior: A shake stores an intensity, duration, source position and radius, and occupies one of four slots, with new ones dropped when all are busy. Each frame the game takes the strongest active shake, multiplied by one minus distance over radius and a linear time fade, and limits the result to 1. It drives three sine waves: pitch with 18 degrees at about 6.7 hertz, yaw with 16 degrees at 12.5 hertz and roll with 10 degrees at 10 hertz. The time fade is applied again to the amplitude, so shakes die out quickly. Large enemy footsteps use 0.08 intensity for 500 milliseconds at 800 units; falls use 0.03 to 0.08 for 200 milliseconds at 200 units. A level-driven rumble scale can replace the strongest shake. The angles are added to the view orientation.

cards.name: Whole-world save with run-length encoding
cards.summary: A save writes the live world state in one pass, compresses runs of zero bytes, and writes through a temp file.
cards.behavior: Saving is refused when the player is dead or the game is not single player. The file starts with a version number (18), the map name, level time, play time and episode, a text summary of 256 characters, music and skill. It then writes every in-use entity, every client and every AI state, field by field. Blocks are packed with a one-byte header: the low seven bits give a run length of up to 127, and the high bit marks the run as zeros, which are not stored. The file goes to a temporary name and is renamed to the target, then copied to the current slot. Loading checks the version against a short list of older ones, restores skill, counts a new attempt and stamps the load time so AI ignores the player for two seconds. Fields may only be appended to structures.

constants.name: run length bytes
constants.unit: bytes per run header, 7 bits for the count

cards.name: Event-driven AI scripts with veto hooks
cards.summary: Each AI can run map-authored action lists on named events, and a script can deny the default reaction to take control.
cards.behavior: A map script file attaches blocks to named events: spawn, trigger, enemy sight, pain, death, state change, bullet impact, sound inspection and more. When the game raises an event it looks for the first block whose parameter matches, by case-insensitive string or, for pain, by a health threshold that the hit crossed, meaning it lies above the new health and at most the previous health, and switches to it. Actions run in order each think, up to 64 per block. An action that returns false blocks the list until done, as with walk to marker or wait. Several events, such as state change, sound inspection and bullet impact, run first and let the script deny the built-in reaction, so designers can replace default behavior. A script can also disable senses or attacking, change attributes, spawn characters, save the game, and fire triggers.

constants.name: scripting pause after hearing a sound
scripting pause after a bullet impact
